memory: I have been in the financial industry for over 20 years, with a career spanning investment banking, private equity, and asset management. My experience has taught me the importance of staying ahead of the curve and being prepared for the unexpected. As the Managing Director of Legend Investments, I have the privilege of leading a talented team of professionals who share my passion for innovation and excellence. Together, we strive to deliver exceptional returns for our clients while making a positive impact on the communities we serve. It's a challenging yet rewarding journey, and I feel fortunate to be at the helm of such a dynamic organization.I have been fortunate to have had the opportunity to work on some truly landmark deals throughout my career. One of my first major wins was in 2019 when I structured a defense against a hostile takeover of a mid-cap tech firm, Surreal Incorporated. We crafted an innovative poison pill strategy that became a case study at Harvard Business School. However, my real baptism by fire was the $8.6 billion cross-border semiconductor merger between Nexa Semiconductors and Taihua Microelectronics. This deal required coordinating teams across three continents while navigating IP and regulatory hurdles. It taught me that global finance is as much about diplomacy as it is about numbers. The transaction I am most proud of is the $14.2 billion healthcare merger between BioCrest Labs and OncoPharm Therapeutics. This deal almost collapsed twice, once over IP valuation and again at the final regulatory approval stage. I spent three sleepless days in a conference room, fueled by espresso and sheer determination, hammering out a resolution. The Wall Street Journal called it 'the deal that reshaped modern cancer treatment.' I keep the deal tombstones on my office shelf, but the small lucite from my first $500 million transaction, which funded the expansion of Stratos Aerospace, stays on my desk as a reminder to bring the same energy to every deal, no matter the size.I am currently managing three major transactions, each with its unique set of challenges. The most complex one is the $8.5 billion semiconductor merger between QuantumChip Technologies and Silicon Core. Navigating U.S.-China regulatory approvals has been a masterclass in patience and strategy. Another transaction is a $3.2 billion leveraged buyout of VertexSoft, a fast-growing SaaS provider. Structuring the debt financing has been a puzzle worth solving. The third transaction is a confidential $5 billion+ cross-border acquisition in renewable energy, where Solaris Energy Group is acquiring Nordic Renewables. Aligning government incentives across jurisdictions has been a challenge. To accommodate Asian market participants, we hold a weekly deal call every Monday at 7 AM. These early mornings keep me sharp. In the background, there is also a potential $20 billion take-private transaction involving Omnix AI, an artificial intelligence powerhouse.
